DARHT Facility During the DARHT WE construction, significant spalling and cracking of the existing DARHT camera/diagnostics room concrete structure was observed. LANL engineers collaborated with the Army Corps of Engineers and the Texas A&M Transportation Institute regarding the condition of the concrete. Core samples were taken from DARHT’s concrete structures and roof for petrographic analysis and alkali-silica reaction (ASR) tests. Based on concrete pour data and the analysis of the core samples, the concrete was identified as being susceptible to freeze/thaw and/or ASR damage, both of which have the potential for long-term negative impacts on structural concrete. In the near term, to minimize the progression of ASR, an epoxy mois- ture barrier was applied to specific roof areas to minimize moisture intrusion and increase the service life of the structure. Permanent repairs will include removal and replacement of firing point roof concrete and installation of a waterproof membrane, combined with repainting the entire facility. These repairs will reduce water intrusion into the concrete structure and will mitigate both dam- age mechanisms. In addition, the concrete pad inside the WE has significant elevation variations that will be addressed to meliorate camera house leveling and allow camera house rail installation, facilitating experiment reconfiguration.
